content: 1. The use of oral antiviral agents, specifically nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, was associated with a significant reduction in all-cause mortality at 28 days, with a risk ratio of 0.08 (95% CI: 0.01 to 0.41). Similarly, molnupiravir demonstrated a risk ratio of 0.04 (95% CI: 0.00 to 0.68) for the same outcome. 2. For COVID-19-related hospitalizations within 28 days, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir showed a risk ratio of 0.11 (95% CI: 0.01 to 0.86), while molnupiravir had a risk ratio of 0.30 (95% CI: 0.05 to 1.73). 3. When considering the combined outcome of COVID-19-related hospitalizations or all-cause death within 28 days, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir had a risk ratio of 0.12 (95% CI: 0.06 to 0.26), and molnupiravir had a risk ratio of 0.69 (95% CI: 0.48 to 1.00). 4. Regarding serious adverse events, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir demonstrated a risk ratio of 0.12 (95% CI: 0.06 to 0.25), while molnupiravir showed a risk ratio of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.49 to 0.99). 5. For serious adverse events specifically attributed to the drug or placebo, nirmatrelvir/ritonavir had a risk ratio of 0.28 (95% CI: 0.18 to 0.43), and molnupiravir had a risk ratio of 0.24 (95% CI: 0.15 to 0.41). 6. The risk of requiring any respiratory intervention by day 29 was reduced with molnupiravir, with a risk ratio of 0.66 (95% CI: 0.45 to 0.96). 7. For the combined outcome of invasive mechanical ventilation (MV), noninvasive MV, or high-flow oxygen device use, molnupiravir showed a risk ratio of 0.47 (95% CI: 0.23 to 0.96). 8. Specifically for invasive mechanical ventilation alone, molnupiravir demonstrated a risk ratio of 0.36 (95% CI: 0.11 to 1.12).
